name: @wave-av/mcp-server
purpose: WAVE is media infrastructure for the agentic internet: one call shape moves live and on-demand media across every transport, and both kinds of user, people and agents, discover it, call it, and pay for it per call. This package is how an agent discovers and calls that call shape over MCP. The hosted server answers at https://mcp.wave.online/mcp, the agent card is published at https://gateway.wave.online/.well-known/agent-card.json, and the skills index at https://gateway.wave.online/.well-known/wave-skills.json. `npx @wave-av/mcp-server` runs a WAVE MCP server locally over stdio for Claude Code, Cursor, and Windsurf.

capabilities.does: List all streams in the WAVE account with pagination and status filtering.
Create a new stream (protocol, recording, region options).
Start a stream by ID, transitioning it to the active state.
Stop an active stream by ID.
Get real-time stream health metrics (bitrate, frame rate, latency).
List all studio productions in the WAVE account.
Create a new multi-camera studio production.
Get current viewer count and viewer demographics for a stream or account-wide.
Get detailed stream performance metrics (bitrate, latency, quality, error rates).
Get current subscription plan, billing cycle, and feature entitlements.
Get current billing-period usage (streaming minutes, storage, bandwidth).
Switch the live program output to a different camera/source in a Cloud Switcher session.
Create a clip from a recorded stream, optionally exporting to social platforms.
Show, hide, or update an HTML5 graphics overlay on a production.
Control a PTZ camera (pan, tilt, zoom, focus, preset recall/store).
Moderate a chat message in a live stream (block, flag, or allow).
Start real-time captions/transcription on a stream.
Mark a moment in a stream as a highlight for later clipping.
Drive a full headless conversation with the WAVE voice agent (WAV in, PCM reply out, no browser/WebRTC).
Run @wave-av/pen-extract's `all` pipeline on a .pen board; returns the manifest (files, sha256s, owed).
Compose and validate a design-contract.json from an extract dir; returns the validator line and key counts.
Run @wave-av/loc-study's `measure` on an image (masked by geometry) or a rasterized plate SVG.
Validate an existing design-contract.json against the schema and acceptance-tests catalogue, no compose.

Deprecated (use wave_compose): propose a WAVE media pipeline (captions/clips/dub/realtime/...) for a goal stated in plain language, grounded in a bundled products/skills/mcp-tools snapshot. Never executes; makes no network request.

Propose a WAVE media pipeline for a goal stated in plain language. Calls the live gateway POST /v1/compose when WAVE_API_KEY is configured; falls back to the same bundled products/skills/mcp-tools snapshot as wave.ask when no key is set or the live call fails. Never executes.

sections.heading: Setup
sections.body:
### 1. Get an API key

```bash
# Via CLI
wave auth login

# Or create at https://console.wave.online/dashboard#keys
```

### 2. Configure your AI tool

Add to your `.mcp.json` (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.) — see the Quick start config above.

sections.heading: Design tools
sections.body: Thin wrappers over the design-to-engineer pipeline's two standalone libraries (`@wave-av/pen-extract`, `@wave-av/loc-study`). Neither library is published to npm yet, so each tool resolves its library from a sibling checkout, $HOME-first, with an env override. Every path argument is confined to `$HOME/wave-av` or the OS temp dir — a call outside those roots is rejected before anything runs.

sections.heading: In-process (Claude Agent SDK) mode
Setup for other AI tools
Troubleshooting
sections.body:
### Server not starting

Verify your API key is set:

```bash
echo $WAVE_API_KEY
```

### Tools not appearing

Restart your AI tool after adding the MCP configuration. Most tools require a restart to detect new MCP servers.

### Connection errors

The MCP server uses stdio transport (no network listener). If you see connection errors, check that `npx` can run successfully:

```bash
npx @wave-av/mcp-server --version
```

### Testing the server

Send a JSON-RPC initialize request to verify:

```bash
echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test","version":"1.0.0"}}}' | npx @wave-av/mcp-server
```
